raw.details:
Overview:

  • Task: Design, fabricate and operate a wireless combat robot capable of safely competing against other teams inside a controlled combat arena.
  • RoboWars evaluates engineering design, reliability, driving skill, weapon effectiveness, strategy and safety compliance.
  • The competition will feature separate 8 kg and 15 kg combat robotics categories.

Eligibility & Team Composition:

  • Teams may consist of up to 8 members.
  • Inter-college teams are allowed.
  • Inter-specialization and cross-year teams are allowed, subject to overall event eligibility.
  • Each team must nominate a Team Captain/Representative for official communication.
  • A maximum of 2 authorized team members may be present in the designated driver area during a match.

Competition Format:

  • The default tournament format will be Double Elimination, unless otherwise announced by the organising committee.
  • Fixtures will be prepared by the organisers/judges.
  • Each standard match will consist of 3 minutes of active fight time, excluding official time-outs.
  • If neither robot achieves a Knockout or Technical Knockout within the allotted time, the winner will be decided by the judges.
  • Robots are expected to actively engage during matches.

Robot Specifications:

8 kg Category:

  • Maximum Weight: 8.00 kg
  • Weight Tolerance: 0%

15 kg Category:

  • Maximum Weight: 15.00 kg
  • Weight Tolerance: 0%

For both categories:

  • Cluster/multibot configurations are allowed, provided their combined weight remains within the category limit.
  • Batteries, armour, weapons, onboard control hardware and pneumatic/hydraulic systems are included in the robot weight.
  • The hand-held transmitter is excluded.
  • A functional active weapon is compulsory. Purely passive wedge/pusher robots are not permitted.
  • Robots must operate using wireless control.
  • Maximum electrical potential permitted on the robot is 51 V DC.

Weapon Specifications:

  • Permitted weapon concepts may include:
    • Spinners
    • Drums
    • Discs/Bars
    • Hammers
    • Saws/Cutters
    • Lifters
    • Flippers
    • Crushers
    • Other systems approved during technical inspection
  • Spinning weapons must be capable of stopping within 60 seconds after power is removed.
  • All hazardous weapon surfaces must have suitable safety covers outside the arena.
  • A proper weapon lock/restraint must be fitted whenever the robot is outside the combat arena.

Prohibited Weapons & Systems:

  • Firearms and explosives
  • Flame/incendiary weapons
  • Solid or liquid projectiles intended to leave the robot
  • Hazardous or corrosive chemicals
  • Electrical shock weapons
  • RF jammers or deliberate communication interference
  • Unsafe entanglement systems
  • Any mechanism considered an unacceptable safety risk by the judges

Control & Safety Requirements:

  • A clearly accessible mechanical kill switch/removable link must isolate power to both the drivetrain and weapon systems.
  • Software-only emergency shutdown is not sufficient as the primary kill mechanism.
  • Loss of radio communication must automatically place the robot in a safe state.
  • Batteries must be securely mounted and protected against electrical and mechanical damage.
  • Robots may only be activated inside the arena, approved testing areas or with explicit permission from organisers.
  • Weapon testing is prohibited in ordinary pit areas.
  • Every robot must pass a technical and safety inspection before competing.

Pneumatic & Hydraulic Systems:

  • Only non-flammable gases may be used in pneumatic systems.
  • Maximum pneumatic working/outlet pressure: 25 bar, subject to component ratings.
  • Maximum hydraulic working pressure: 50 bar, subject to component ratings.
  • Pressure vessels, regulators and associated systems must be securely mounted and appropriately rated.
  • The complete pneumatic/hydraulic system must remain onboard during the match.
  • Teams may be required to provide relevant safety or certification documentation.

Match Regulations:

  • Robots may begin moving only after the official start signal.
  • Pinning or lifting an opponent may be maintained for a maximum of 10 seconds, after which the attacking robot must release when instructed.
  • A robot may be declared immobilized if it cannot demonstrate meaningful controlled translational movement during a 10-second count.
  • Teams may concede through an official tap-out/forfeit procedure.
  • Deliberate attacks after a tap-out, match-stop instruction or final signal may result in immediate disqualification.
  • Only authorised event officials may enter the arena during an active match or safety incident.

Judging Criteria:

If a match goes to a judges' decision, robots will be evaluated based on:

  • Aggression – frequency, intent, effectiveness and severity of attacks.
  • Damage – functional damage deliberately caused to the opponent.
  • Control – ability to dictate engagements, manoeuvre effectively, utilise weapons and minimise incoming damage.

The decision of the Head Judge/Organising Committee will be final.

Technical Inspection:

Before entering the competition, robots may be checked for:

  • Weight compliance
  • Mechanical kill switch
  • Radio fail-safe
  • Weapon lock
  • Battery installation
  • Structural integrity
  • Pneumatic/hydraulic safety
  • Sharp-edge protection
  • Compliance with the submitted robot specifications

Robots may be re-inspected after repairs, modifications or significant combat damage.

General Rules:

  • Unsafe robots may be stopped or disqualified at any stage.
  • Teams must immediately follow instructions issued by referees and event officials.
  • Physical violence, threats, harassment, serious verbal abuse or unsporting behaviour may result in penalties or disqualification.
  • Any unusual mechanism or system not clearly covered by the rulebook must receive prior approval.
  • The organising committee reserves the right to modify schedules, fixtures, inspection procedures or rules when required for safety and smooth conduct of the event.

Ready to enter the arena?:

Build smart. Fight hard. Survive the battle.

ROBOWARS 2026

Build. Battle. Dominate.
